title: What is PostgreSQL?
description: Discover PostgreSQL's architecture, 35-year evolution from Ingres, ACID guarantees, and object-relational capabilities.

data.text: **PostgreSQL** (frequently referred to as Postgres) is an enterprise-grade, open-source object-relational database management system (ORDBMS). Originating from the POSTGRES project directed by Professor Michael Stonebraker at UC Berkeley in 1986, it has undergone more than 35 years of active engineering.

data.title: Why PostgreSQL Dominates Modern Infrastructure
items: **Full ACID Compliance**: Strong transactional guarantees with customizable isolation levels (Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable).
**Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC)**: Readers do not block writers, and writers do not block readers.
**Unmatched Extensibility**: Support for custom data types, user-defined operators, procedural languages (PL/pgSQL, PL/Python, PL/v8), and extensions like PostGIS and pgvector.
**Hybrid Relational and Document (JSONB)**: First-class support for unstructured JSON documents with binary indexing (GIN) and json-path operators.

terms.definition: Object-Relational Database Management System — combines traditional relational table structures with object-oriented capabilities like inheritance and custom types.
Multi-Version Concurrency Control — a concurrency mechanism where each transaction sees a consistent snapshot of data without holding shared read locks.
A persistence technique where all data file modifications are recorded sequentially in a write log before being flushed to database heap pages.

data.title: Pronunciation & Naming
data.text: The official pronunciation is 'post-gress-Q-L'. While often called 'Postgres' casually, both terms refer to the same open-source engine.
A Short History That Explains the Design

PostgreSQL began as the **POSTGRES** research project at UC Berkeley in 1986, led by Michael Stonebraker. The team replaced its own query language with SQL in 1994 and renamed the project **PostgreSQL** to signal that change. In 1996 the project moved to an open, community-run development model that it still uses today: no single company owns the code, and every feature goes through public mailing-list review.

The practical consequence is a database that prefers **correctness over shortcuts**. When PostgreSQL added JSON support it did so as a genuine storage type with its own indexes rather than a text column with string matching. That conservatism is why banks, and later startups and AI teams, trust it.

rows: Custom types, operators, index methods, extensions

data.text: Interviewers rarely want you to declare a winner. They want to hear the **reasoning**: PostgreSQL wins when you need correctness, rich types, or one engine instead of five; MySQL is often simpler to operate at small scale; SQL Server is common in Microsoft shops and has tighter tooling integration.
What MVCC Actually Means for You

**Multi-Version Concurrency Control** means an `UPDATE` never overwrites a row in place. Instead PostgreSQL writes a new row version and marks the old one dead. Because every statement works against a consistent snapshot, a long analytical `SELECT` will not be blocked by, and will not block, concurrent writers.

The trade-off is that dead row versions accumulate and must be reclaimed by `VACUUM`. That single design decision explains a huge share of everyday PostgreSQL operations: bloat, autovacuum tuning, and transaction ID wraparound.

data.title: What Interviewers Look For
data.text: When asked "What is PostgreSQL?", cover three things: (1) it is a **process-per-connection** database, not thread-per-connection; (2) it uses **MVCC** so reads and writes do not block each other; (3) it is **extensible**, which is why the same engine now handles JSON, geospatial, vector, and time-series workloads.

data.title: Explore a Live Instance
data.description: Spend ten minutes on a real instance instead of reading about one.
steps: Start a container: `docker run -d --name pgdemo -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret -p 5432:5432 postgres:16`.
Connect with `psql -h localhost -U postgres` and run `SELECT version();`.
Create a table, insert a JSONB row, and query it with the `->>` operator.
Open a second terminal, start `BEGIN; UPDATE ...` and leave it open. In the first terminal the row is still readable — that is MVCC in action.
data.expectedOutcome: You can explain from first-hand observation why a writer did not block a reader.

items.question: Is PostgreSQL pronounced "post-gress" or "post-gress-Q-L"?
items.answer: Both are accepted. The core team uses "post-gress-Q-L", and "Postgres" is the widely used shorthand.

items.question: Is PostgreSQL object-relational or just relational?
items.answer: It is object-relational: it supports table inheritance, composite and range types, custom types, and operators in addition to the relational model.

items.question: Why is PostgreSQL so popular for new startups?
items.answer: One engine covers relational data, documents, search, geospatial, and vectors, so a small team avoids operating five different datastores.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PostgreSQL is an open-source, object-relational database under the permissive PostgreSQL License — no vendor lock-in.
It has been in development since 1986 and follows a transparent, community-run release process with five-year support per major version.
MVCC lets readers and writers work concurrently, at the cost of needing regular `VACUUM` to reclaim dead row versions.
Its extension ecosystem (PostGIS, pgvector, TimescaleDB, JSONB) turns one database into a multi-modal platform.
data.takeaway: Say "MVCC, extensibility, and correctness" and you have answered the interview question before the follow-ups start.
